fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: some notes added (most probably by K. D. MacDonald?). See below for details.]

item.description: a superstitious person.
mushrooms.

“Latha Fheill Padruig, leth an earraich, thig an niomhair as an talamh, cha bhith mise ris an niomhair, ’s cha mhotha bhios an niomhair ruim [sic].” The reference to the serpent is unclear to me and the informant cannot shed light on its significance.
“Biodh gach neach a’ toirt sgairbh a creagan dha fhein.” – let everyone fend for themselves.
having tea without sitting at a table, e.g. “An gabh thu tì na’d laimh.”
a mischievous child who does not heed advice or censure.
death without blemish.
not sure of exact date but arises between Christmas and New Year.
“’S ioma rud a tha an cois a’ laoigh nach saoill a mhàthair.” – a proverb which refers to the unpredictability of someone you might trust implicitly.
“Nuair a bhios a’ pobull gann ni an gille càm ministear.”
“’S fhearr duine gun ni na ni gun duine.”
“Nuair a thig latha thig comhairle.”
a church.
a bannock that was not properly shaped, not rounded.
“Fhuair e gabhail aige.” – he was well treated.
“’S fhearr suathadh ri crois na fuathal ri crois.”
“’S fhearr an cù a dh’fhalbhas na an cù a dh’fhuiricheas.” – the more versatile you are the better chance you have of survival.
“’S leatha na ròn tònn eadar a thaigh.” – refers to the obesity which might strike someone who was eternally visiting houses. [NOTES: ‘tònn’ corrected to ‘tòn’.]
“’S math a bhean taighe a bheir a nuas a rud nach eil shuas.”
according to the informant red wool was needed to make a successful ‘snàthla’. For description of ‘snàthla’ see earlier notes.
corner of the mouth. [NOTES: ‘beoil’ corrected to ‘beòil’.]
to conquer. [NOTES: corrected to ‘cothach(ach)adh’.]
throwing people off as in a skirmish.
a quagmire of mud and dirt which could pull you down.
an old word which referred to strong liquer [sic] [liquor?] of any kind. Informant has a song on this. [NOTES: note added above – Di-abhlam.]
knowledgeable, skilful.
noise, shouting, consternation.
“’S fhearr fuine thana na bhi uile falamh.”
a witch. [NOTES: a note added above – muileartach.]
something that is cumbersome and difficult to operate. Actually this was in reference to my recording machine!
a rich, opulent stream. [NOTES: ‘strùthan’ corrected to ‘struthan’.]
a cellar.
“Cha be daoine an t-aodach, ’s cha be a cholunn bhreugach.” – a proverb which refers to the outward artificial appearance of someone. It is his inner personality which counts.
Tòmhseachan: “Ceithir a ruidh, ceithir air chrith, ’s dithis a’ deanamh an rathaid, ’s fear ag éigheach.” Refers to different parts of a cow – legs, teats, eyes and mouth.
the lowing sound of cattle.
a small bundle, in this instance a small bundle of wool. [NOTES: corrected to ‘tapan’.]
when carding this was the amount of wool laid flat on the card.
black roots were boiled. Wool steeped in this to give a black colour.
added to the wool so that it would be easier to work with. This was done prior to carding.
forever. [NOTES: note added above ‘um’ in ‘dìlum’ – eann.]
debts. Could also be interpreted as sins.
surrounding.
particular type of humiliation as a result of intimidation by your oppressors.
